1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, London Defensive System

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.strategy: Completes the kingside fianchetto and clears the way to castling; the queen's bishop follows to the long diagonal next. White controls the centre from a distance with pieces, as the opening intends, while Black's f5 bishop is already developed outside the chain.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, London Defensive System

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bb2.strategy: Brings the queen's bishop to the long diagonal at once, aiming at e5 and the black kingside, and delays the king's bishop. It is the other order of the same fianchetto set-up, at the cost of keeping the king in the centre a move longer.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bb2.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, London Defensive System

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 c6 3.g3 Nf6 4.b3 Bf5 5.Bg2.strategy: Black gets a complete, solid set-up before White's second bishop arrives: d5 is safe, the f8-bishop is free to develop, and the bishop on f5 stays outside the pawn chain.
